newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major wouldn't get job selling insurance-poll.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major wouldn't get job selling insurance-poll.

text.p: If British premier John Major finds himself looking for a new job after next week's election, he'd best not consider a career selling life insurance, if the results of a new poll are to be believed.

A survey of 1,000 by UK insurer Cornhill Life aimed at identifying the kind of people they should recruit as sales staff showed only 14 per cent of men and 12 per cent of women would feel happy buying an insurance policy from him.
Labour leader Tony Blair fared only slightly better in the poll, securing the confidence of 20 percent of men and 17 percent of women, while Paddy Ashdown scored equal votes to John Major.
Cornhill Life's general manager Ian Reed said he would be reluctant to offer any of them a job.
"I am afraid none of the party leaders would be able to convert enough leads into sales to justify the offer of a position," he said.
"The prime minister never believes what the polls say," said a spokesman at the Conservative party headquarters.
"But we are confident he will not be looking for a new job."
